rules.sentence: Dedifferentiated SFT; a. Abrupt transition of conventional SFT areas with high grade sarcomatous areas with, b. marked nuclear pleomorphism and increased mitoses
The dedifferentiated variant is extremely rare and shows abrupt transition to a low or high-grade sarcoma with adjacent conventional SFT.
Different clinical and histomorphological features have been described which are suggestive of malignancy.
These features include older age, larger tumor size, increased cellularity, increased mitotic activity (≥4/10HPFs or > 2mitoses/2 mm2), nuclear pleomorphism, tumor necrosis and infiltrative borders.
Tumors lacking malignant histological features in primary resection specimens may acquire malignant features at time of recurrence and metastases.
